title: Finite local-factor decomposition of a commutative Artinian ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity. Assume $R$ is Artinian, meaning that every descending chain of ideals stabilizes. Then there exist a finite set $I$, nonzero commutative Artinian local rings $R_i$ for $i\in I$, and an isomorphism of unital rings $R\simeq\prod_{i\in I}R_i$. Here local means having a unique maximal ideal [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-idempotent-zero-one]. The zero ring is included: its decomposition has $I=\varnothing$, with empty product the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 00KJ, proposition-dimension-zero-ring, equivalence (1) and (4); local factors are nonzero by the definition of a local ring.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00KJ (proposition-dimension-zero-ring), (1) implies (4), via 00J7, 00J8 and 00JA; direct Mathlib realization specified in mathlib_match.

Finiteness is IsArtinianRing.instFiniteMaximalSpectrum, Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:525-527. Each factor is Artinian by IsArtinianRing.localization_artinian, Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Ring.lean:92-93 (or its concrete Localization instance at 97-98), and local by Localization.AtPrime.isLocalRing, Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/AtPrime/Basic.lean:107-108. For R = 0 the maximal spectrum is empty and the same equivalence gives the empty product. Source read 2026-10-24.
